LESSON: MELODY

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Melody

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Melody. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify melodic variations in familiar simple tunes demonstrating an awareness of pitch and rhythm, familiar tunes (4 to 8 bars long),
2. create melodic variations to familiar tunes in preparation for composition,
3. apply variations of tempo and dynamics to familiar songs for enjoyment,
4. use new words to a familiar tune for effective communication, e) create own melodic patterns from differently pitched pitched objects such as voice and objects to enhance creativity, f) use digital devices in creating and recording own created melodic patterns for digital literacy and presentation to other for discussions. 352 Property of the Government of Kenya compositions to the rest of the class and as a group discuss the compositions. create and record own melodic patterns and discuss giving ideas for modification.

Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Melody.
2. Explain Melody to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Melody.
4. Show that you can: identify melodic variations in familiar simple tunes demonstrating an awareness of pitch and rhythm, familiar tunes (4 to 8 bars long),
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Melody. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Melody important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. identify melodic variations in familiar simple tunes demonstrating an awareness of pitch and rhythm, familiar tunes (4 to 8 bars long),
2. create melodic variations to familiar tunes in preparation for composition,
3. apply variations of tempo and dynamics to familiar songs for enjoyment,
4. use new words to a familiar tune for effective communication, e) create own melodic patterns from differently pitched pitched objects such as voice and objects to enhance creativity, f) use digital devices in creating and recording own created melodic patterns for digital literacy and presentation to other for discussions. 352 Property of the Government of Kenya compositions to the rest of the class and as a group discuss the compositions. create and record own melodic patterns and discuss giving ideas for modification.
